# Appendix D Data and Preparation of the Experimental Instances

## D1 Data sources and scope

An experimental instance combines a facility population, supply and demand
over time, investment and operating costs, capacity rules, road distances and
an uncertainty design. This appendix describes these inputs and the
transformations needed to reproduce the evaluated model.

The reference is the
[gold workbook, model_agrologistic_padrao_ouro.xlsx](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/templates/model_agrologistic_padrao_ouro.xlsx).
It supplies the model schema, supply and demand records, costs and a
215-facility population. Additional candidate locations come from
Warehouses_Existing_Candidate_All.xlsx, whose version and structure are
identified in the [registry manifest](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/manifests/warehouse_population_source_v020.json).
The two sources have different roles: the gold workbook defines the reference
instance; the registry provides potential additions to its candidate set.

The [version 0.2.0 dataset](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22751909)
and its
[input archive](https://zenodo.org/records/22751909/files/agrologistic-v020-inputs.zip?download=1)
provide the deposited source material, subject to the stated file-level access
and reuse conditions. The gold workbook is also directly available from GitHub.
The external registry and ignored processed workbooks are not embedded in the
Git repository. Full file identities, worksheet inventories and experimental
input paths are listed in the
[input reproduction guide](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/appendix_input_reproduction_20261028.json).
Readers should compare those identities before using a downloaded workbook;
a matching filename or facility count alone does not identify an input.

The gold workbook contains 14 worksheets and 215 facility records:
146 existing warehouses and 69 candidates. Its Warehouses sheet has 25 columns.
The registry has 18,086 facility records and 13 columns: 146 existing sites
and 17,940 candidates. One candidate with nonpositive static capacity is
excluded from the eligible selection pool.

The effective model contains 37 origin identifiers, 27 domestic destination
roles, ten export roles, two products and 60 planning periods. An identifier
denotes a model entity; coincident coordinates do not merge entities.
A destination may have both domestic and export roles, so the ten export
records should not be interpreted as ten distinct physical ports.

## D2 Quantities and units

Supply and demand are read from Oferta and Demanda. Each record identifies
a product, location, period and quantity. Facility records use CDA as the
identifier; names and coordinates are descriptive attributes. The input reader
aggregates additive supply or demand entries that share the same effective
keys. Missing mandatory identifiers are treated as input errors. Initial
inventory is zero where no initial-stock record is supplied.

| Quantity | Meaning | Effective unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supply and domestic demand | Grain available or required in a product-period record | t/period |
| Export limit | Upper bound on optional arrivals at an export destination | t/period |
| Initial inventory and static capacity | Grain held at a warehouse | t |
| Reception and shipping rates | Grain that can be handled each operating day | t/day |
| Freight coefficient | Cost multiplied by grain quantity and directed road distance | BRL/(t km) |
| Inventory holding | Cost per unit held in a planning period | BRL/(t period) |
| Capacity investment | Fixed cost and cost per investment-tonne, according to facility eligibility | BRL and BRL/t |

: Table D.1. Units used in the experimental model.

Static capacity limits inventory, whereas reception and shipping limit flows
within a period. The experiments use 30 operating days per period. Candidate
and expansion investments add daily reception and shipping capacity at a rate
of 0.20 per investment-tonne. Bulk-handling conversion uses a factor of 1.0
and adds handling capacity without adding static storage.

Two actual gold-workbook records illustrate these distinctions. Existing
facility CDA 35.0287.0002-6 has static capacity 890 t, reception 5 t/day and
shipping 6 t/day. Its period reception and shipping limits are therefore
150 t and 180 t before eligible investment effects. Candidate
CDA 79.G590.0003-9 has zero base capacity in all three categories and an
investment upper bound of 307079 t. That bound is neither installed capacity
nor an investment chosen by the optimizer. These values illustrate input
interpretation, not observed grain movements.

The [Excel reader](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/excel_loader.py) and
[mathematical input contract](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/mathematical_contract.py)
implement the unit conventions and transformations. Facility-specific
eligibility and maxima take precedence over general fallback values.

## D3 Investment, operating costs and penalty coefficients

Table D.2 reports the investment cost schedule used when a facility has no
explicit effective coefficient. The average of each low/high pair provides
the corresponding fallback. An explicit facility coefficient is retained
instead of replacing every facility by a common average.

| Investment type | Low/high source values, BRL/t | Fallback coefficient, BRL/t |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| New conventional warehouse | 1000 / 1500 | 1250 |
| New metal silo | 785 / 1310 | 1047.5 |
| Existing-site expansion | 600 / 1200 | 900 |
| Bulk-handling conversion | 380 / 660 | 520 |

: Table D.2. Investment cost schedule and arithmetic-mean fallback coefficients.

The candidate-cost fallback uses the conventional-warehouse value of
1250 BRL/t. Where a candidate has a total investment estimate and a positive
maximum capacity, the capacity-proportional coefficient is obtained by
dividing that estimate by the maximum capacity, with the corresponding fixed
component set to zero. The same project estimate is consequently not charged
again as an additional fixed cost. The general expansion limit is 0.25 of
static capacity when no facility-specific maximum is supplied.

Inventory-holding tariffs are 45 BRL/(t period) for soybean and
48 BRL/(t period) for corn, for both public and private operators. The
additional Outros tariff in the source does not create a third product in
the evaluated instances.

| State code(s) | Source freight coefficient, BRL/(t km) |
| --- | ---: |
| MT | 0.1842 |
| AM | 0.1969 |
| PE | 0.2004 |
| MS | 0.2174 |
| BA | 0.2584 |
| AC, AL, AP, CE, ES, PA, PB, RJ, RN, RR, SE | 0.2648 |
| DF | 0.294 |
| MA | 0.2943 |
| PI | 0.2979 |
| PR | 0.312 |
| SP | 0.3279 |
| RO | 0.3346 |
| RS | 0.3408 |
| GO | 0.3682 |
| TO | 0.3826 |
| MG | 0.3971 |
| SC | 0.4014 |

: Table D.3. Actual Frete!A2:B28 values in the registered gold workbook.


Transport cost is calculated from grain quantity, the applicable state freight
coefficient and directed road distance. These coefficients are a declared
cost approximation, rather than observed prices for each road movement.

The scalar objective uses three artificial coefficients: 90000 BRL per tonne
of unmet domestic demand, 45000 BRL per tonne of static exceedance in each
period, and 45000 BRL per tonne of reception overflow. They are identical
across the reported scalar experiments. Static exceedance summed across
periods is expressed in tonne-periods; reception overflow is already a period
flow and is not multiplied by operating days again.

These weights allow the optimizer to trade investment and operation against
specified shortages or exceedances. They are not calibrated economic damages.
Financial expenditure and artificial penalties are therefore reported
separately. A small gap for their sum does not establish the same relative
accuracy for the financial subtotal or a particular domestic service level.

All monetary results are in Brazilian reais over the 60-period horizon,
without a newly imposed currency conversion, price-year adjustment,
annualization or discount rate. The
[parameter guide](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/appendix_input_reproduction_20261028.json)
retains the complete numerical mapping to the effective model.

## D4 Warehouse populations

The h215 reference population contains 146 existing facilities and 69
candidate anchors. Larger instances retain these facilities and add candidates
from a deterministic, proportionally stratified ranking of the eligible
registry. Strata use state, facility type and static-capacity quartile.
The selection seed and ordered memberships are retained with the
[population lineage](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h300_population_lineage_20261020.json).

| Instance | Existing facilities | Candidate options | Candidates added beyond h215 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| h215 | 146 | 69 | 0 |
| h300 | 146 | 154 | 85 |
| h400 | 146 | 254 | 185 |
| h500 | 146 | 354 | 285 |

: Table D.4. Facility populations available to the optimization.

The [population selector](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/warehouse_population.py)
orders the eligible candidates. The
[workbook constructor](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/warehouse_workbook.py)
retains the canonical rows and materializes the selected additions.
For each new candidate, base static, reception and shipping capacities are
zero. Its positive registry static capacity becomes the maximum investable
capacity. The new candidate has no expansion or bulk-conversion eligibility.
Thus, adding a registry location creates an investment option, not an
already operating warehouse.

The facility sets are nested, but the optimizer's chosen capacities and flows
need not be. In addition, route screening is recalculated for each population;
nested facility membership does not guarantee nested selected arc sets or
feasible regions. Objective and runtime changes therefore cannot be attributed
to warehouse count alone.

## D5 Road distances, network selection and scenarios

OSRM materialization supplies directed road distances for the fixed Brazil
road dataset and driving profile. The retained h215, h300, h400 and h500
workbooks contain respectively 63289, 113269, 190569 and 287869 directed
distance pairs. No Haversine fallback is recorded for these materializations.
The processed workbooks add a Distancias sheet to the gold structure, giving
15 worksheets.

The distance matrix precedes product-specific network selection. The
evaluated sparse policy uses 20% connectivity-preserving Pareto selection
and one export sink per product. Materialized pairs are consequently not
counts of retained arcs or flow variables. Topology W excludes direct
origin-to-destination movement; D includes it in addition to warehouse routes.
Availability of a distance does not itself authorize a flow variable.

STO combines supply multipliers 0.85, 1 and 1.15 with domestic-demand
multipliers 0.95, 1 and 1.05. Their Cartesian product gives nine complete
trajectories, each with probability 1/9. These are controlled scenarios,
rather than empirically estimated event probabilities. DET uses the original
deterministic supply and demand arrays. Investments are shared across the
STO trajectories; operations vary by scenario.

Road lengths determine transport costs but do not supply route polylines.
Geographic figures therefore show the available verified node and investment
locations. Straight lines between nodes are not substituted for actual road
paths. Transport quantities can still be analyzed from exported flows without
claiming a verified geographic path.

## D6 Reproducing an instance

First obtain the source files identified in the
[data contract](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/manifests/mvp_data_contract.json)
and input guide, subject to their access conditions. Compare full file
hashes before processing. The runtime workbook, facility order, road
materialization and experiment definition must belong to the same instance.

The h215 processed workbook is model_input.xlsx under
data/processed/policy_population_v020_osrm/warehouses_215.
The h300, h400 and h500 inputs use warehouses_300, warehouses_400 and
warehouses_500 under data/processed/nine_population_osrm_v1. These identify
retained experimental inputs, rather than files distributed as GitHub source.
A newly generated workbook should be recorded separately; changes in spreadsheet
metadata or recalculated caches can alter its byte identity.

Next verify existing/candidate roles, ordered CDA memberships and the 69
canonical anchors. Reuse the recorded candidate order and OSRM materialization.
A new random draw or routing query creates a different input. Apply the
recorded capacity coupling, terminal-stock rule, route policy, topology and
scenario design. Check the effective coefficients listed above before
constructing the model.

Finally, bind the input to the source version and numerical settings of its
experiment. The original
[h215](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h215_2217990_review.json),
[h300](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h300_2218193_review.json),
[h400](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h400_2219884_review.json) and
[h500](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h500_2220382_review.json)
records identify those versions, inputs and validation results.
The [W/D comparison](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_wd_h215_input_inspection_20261022.json)
documents the common graph and costs for the topology comparison.
Appendix C explains small verification cases and original-unit solution
validation before large results are interpreted.

## D7 Reproduction and evidence limits

Public source code, the gold workbook, data inventories and experiment records
allow inspection of the formulation, effective coefficients and reported
claims. Repeating a large calculation additionally requires access to its
exact processed inputs, a compatible solver and runtime, sufficient resources
and the declared stopping rules.

Rebuilding the article reproduces its document and derived tables; it does
not rerun the optimization. Reviewing an existing certificate checks retained
evidence. A fresh numerical reproduction instead requires newly exported
decisions and independent residual validation. Alternative optima, solver
versions and shared-node conditions can produce different decision vectors
or logs even when objective quality and physical feasibility agree.

Traceability makes these distinctions inspectable. It does not by itself
establish economic calibration, unrestricted data access or reproducibility
under arbitrary computing conditions.
